To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Radon formalism of the magnetic phase shift can be used to reconstruct the 2D components of the magnetic induction vector using iterative tomographic methods.
the magnetic phase shift can be represented as a Radon transformation of the magnetic induction, and the magnetic induction can be reconstructed using iterative methods from the magnetic phase shift.
we present a formalization of the magnetic induction as a Radon Transform, and we demonstrate its application to reconstruct the magnetic induction in a nanowired using iterative methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a new technique for the quantitative 3D reconstruction of magnetic induction from the Lorentz phase contrast image of a nano-magnetic sample.
the reconstruction of the 3-D magnetic induction from Lorentz TEM images.
the reconstruction of 3D magnetic induction vector field using Lorentz TEM.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Lorentz transmission TEM can be used to obtain 3D magnetic induction of the samples with high accuracy and the iterative algorithms can be used to reconstruct the 4D vector field of the magnetization.
iterative reconstruction of the magnetic induction is a feasible and robust method to reconstruct the 2D and 3D magnetic vector fields from the phase images of the sample.
the reconstruction of 3D magnetic induction from the Lorentz transmission tomography data is possible using iterative methods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the magnetic induction can be reconstructed using iterative methods and that the reconstruction is not very sensitive to the missing wedge.

the magnetic induction vector field can be reconstructed from the magnetic phase shift using iterative reconstruction methods, and that these iterative reconstruction methods can be used to reconstruct complex 3D magnetic induction vector fields.
the magnetic induction can be reconstructed from the magnetic phase shift in a similar way as the electron density can be reconstructed from electron intensity using standard tomography methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
iterative methods are very suitable for the reconstruction of the vector magnetic field.
the iterative methods are very effective in the presence of missing wedge, which makes them very suitable for Lorentz TEM tomography.

the magnetic induction vector field of a sample can be reconstructed using common iterative tomographic methods and this can be used to visualize the 3D magnetic vector field in a quantitative manner.
